target.title: fix(ci): run Telegram release QA from trusted harness
target.body:
Fixes #103188

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where release operators validating an older selected ref could run that candidate's Telegram QA harness and scenarios, leaving current regression assertions unproven against the release candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram QA jobs now build the exact selected candidate without secrets, move it outside the trusted workspace, restore and build the harness from `github.workflow_sha`, attest both SHAs, and then run the current harness against the candidate gateway and plugins. Candidate scripts are restricted to repository-trusted release provenance: QA All skips same-repo open PR heads, while Release Checks accepts main ancestry, `v*` tags, or exact trusted branch heads, including SHA-pinned `release-ci/*` validation refs.

## User Impact

Release maintainers get current Telegram QA scenarios and assertions against the exact candidate runtime/plugin SHA, with source provenance recorded in the job summary and uploaded artifacts. There is no product runtime change.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` (46/46 + 74/74 passed)
- `actionlint .github/workflows/qa-live-transports-convex.yml .github/workflows/openclaw-release-checks.yml`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- Fresh Codex autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct, confidence 0.84
- Blacksmith Testbox warmup `tbx_01kx4r4x774rrdmfspkv2y17an` initially completed, but its hosted run auto-cancelled before the box could execute tests: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29060990076. The focused tests above used the documented local fallback; hosted exact-head checks remain required.
